tls.certificate_expired.plan: Renew the certificate with your CA, deploy the replacement to every TLS endpoint, and verify the full chain and validity window.

tls.hostname_mismatch.plan: Issue and deploy a certificate whose subjectAltName covers the requested hostname; verify every load balancer and CDN edge.

tls.certificate_untrusted.plan: Deploy the complete leaf and intermediate chain from a publicly trusted CA and remove private or self-signed certificates from public endpoints.

tls.self_signed.plan: Replace the public endpoint certificate with one issued by a publicly trusted CA. Keep self-signed certificates limited to explicitly managed private environments.

tls.weak_cipher.plan: Remove RC4, 3DES, NULL and export cipher suites from the TLS configuration at the origin, load balancer and CDN. Retest negotiated suites after deployment.

tls.certificate_expiring.plan: Renew before expiry and automate renewal monitoring; confirm the renewed certificate is active at all endpoints.

tls.certificate_revoked.plan: Immediately remove the revoked certificate from service, revoke or rotate the affected private key, and install a replacement certificate. Investigate the revocation reason with the issuing CA.

tls.weak_rsa_key.plan: Replace the RSA key with at least 2048-bit RSA or a modern elliptic-curve key and reissue the certificate.

tls.sha1_signature.plan: Reissue the certificate using a modern SHA-256-or-stronger signature algorithm.

tls.legacy_protocol.plan: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in the origin, load balancer, and CDN configuration; retain TLS 1.2 or newer.

dns.no_caa.plan: Publish a restrictive CAA record listing only the certificate authorities authorized to issue for this domain, then verify it at the authoritative DNS provider.

dns.dnssec_missing.plan: Enable DNSSEC signing at the authoritative DNS provider and publish the matching DS record at the parent zone. Confirm validation with a validating resolver.

http.no_https_redirect.plan: Redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS at the edge and preserve the original host and path safely.

http.no_hsts.plan: After confirming HTTPS works across all subdomains, send Strict-Transport-Security with an appropriate max-age; add includeSubDomains only when every subdomain is ready.

http.no_csp.plan: Define a Content-Security-Policy from the application's required sources, test in report-only mode, then enforce it.

http.no_frame_protection.plan: Set frame-ancestors in Content-Security-Policy; use X-Frame-Options for legacy browser compatibility.

http.no_nosniff.plan: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and ensure responses use accurate Content-Type values.

http.no_referrer_policy.plan: Set a Referrer-Policy that limits cross-origin URL disclosure, such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and verify flows that rely on referrer data.

http.no_permissions_policy.plan: Set a Permissions-Policy that disables browser features the application does not need, and allow only origins that require each feature.

http.cookie_insecure.plan: Set Secure and HttpOnly on session cookies and choose an appropriate SameSite policy; validate cross-site flows before rollout.

http.cookie_samesite.plan: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict for same-site session flows; use SameSite=None; Secure only when a cross-site cookie is required and protected by CSRF controls.

http.mixed_content.plan: Serve active page resources over HTTPS, update hard-coded HTTP URLs, and enforce a Content-Security-Policy upgrade-insecure-requests directive after testing.
